cards.text: Solomon, king of Israel, built the house of the LORD in seven years (1 Kings 6:38). His entire palace, though, takes him thirteen years to complete. I've had batches run long, friend, but never THIRTEEN YEARS long.

First comes the House of the Forest of Lebanon, a hall a hundred cubits long, with four rows of cedar pillars holding up cedar beams and three tiers of high windows. Then Solomon builds a colonnade with a portico in front of it.

cards.question: Solomon also builds a hall for his throne, where he will judge.

cards.text: That hall is called the Hall of Justice, and it's paneled with cedar from floor to ceiling. Set further back is the palace where Solomon will live, and he makes a palace like that hall for Pharaoh's daughter, whom he had married. All these buildings are made with costly stones cut to size, and the great courtyard is surrounded by rows of dressed stone and cedar beams.
Now King Solomon sends to bring a man named Huram from Tyre. Friend, I sat in a junk drawer for YEARS, and the only thing anybody ever came looking for was the scissors.

Huram's mother is a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a craftsman in bronze. Huram himself has great skill, understanding and knowledge for every kind of bronze work.

cards.question: Huram comes to King Solomon but goes home before the work is done.

cards.text: Then Huram goes to work, and it's ALL bronze: two tall pillars at the temple's portico named Jachin and Boaz, and a huge round basin called the Sea resting on twelve bronze oxen. He also makes ten stands on wheels with a basin for each, plus pots, shovels and sprinkling bowls.

The king has every piece cast in clay molds in the plain of the Jordan, and Solomon leaves it all unweighed. Nobody ever needed a scale for ME, friend, because I came with a price sticker that said twenty-five cents.

cards.question: Why does Solomon leave all of Huram's bronze pieces unweighed?

answers.text: There were so many of them
The bronze was a gift from Tyre

cards.text: Solomon also makes the furnishings for the house of the LORD, and these are GOLD. The golden altar, the golden table for the Bread of the Presence, ten lampstands of pure gold, lamps, basins, right down to gold hinges on the doors.
So all the work King Solomon does for the house of the LORD is completed. Then he brings in what his father David had dedicated: the silver, the gold and the furnishings.

cards.question: Solomon places David's silver, gold and furnishings in the ___ of the house of the LORD.

cards.text: But friend, don't take your apron off yet. This story is not done.
